q: A C₀-semigroup {S(t)}_{t≥0} on a Banach space satisfies:
opts: S(0)=I, S(t+s)=S(t)S(s), and t↦S(t)x is continuous for each x
S(t) is a group (invertible for all t)
S(t) is compact for all t>0
exp: A C₀ (strongly continuous) semigroup satisfies the semigroup law S(t+s)=S(t)S(s), S(0)=I, and strong continuity t↦S(t)x→x as t→0. The generator A = lim_{t→0}(S(t)x-x)/t is typically unbounded (e.g., the Laplacian for the heat equation).
